title: Missing #[non_exhaustive] on public result structs in mime-tree
description: ParsedPart, ParsedMessage, DecodedBodyValue, and ParsedHeader are all-pub-field structs with no #[non_exhaustive] attribute. Callers can currently write struct literal expressions to construct them directly (e.g. ParsedPart { part_id: ..., children: vec![], ... }). Once any caller does this, adding a field is a breaking API change. These are output/result types — callers have no legitimate reason to construct them. What goes wrong: the next time a field is added to any of these structs (e.g. to expose a new parsed property), semver requires a major version bump even though the field is purely additive. All four structs in mime-tree/src/part.rs and mime-tree/src/message.rs need #[non_exhaustive].
